Read a formula from a DIMACS CNF file

Source: R/dimacs.R
read_dimacs.Rd

DIMACS is the format every SAT solver and benchmark set speaks, so this is usually how a real problem arrives.

Usage

read_dimacs(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a .cnf file.

Value

A list of integer vectors, one per clause, suitable for sat_solve() or sat_solver().

Details

The parser is deliberately lenient about the things files in the wild actually do:

  • clauses may span several lines, and several clauses may share one;

  • the p cnf header is not required, and its counts are not trusted – plenty of files disagree with themselves, and the clauses are the truth;

  • a final clause missing its terminating 0 is still read;

  • a % line ends the file, which is what SATLIB benchmarks use. Without this the 0 that follows it would be read as an empty clause and turn every SATLIB instance unsatisfiable.

See also

write_dimacs()

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".cnf")
write_dimacs(list(c(1, 2), c(-1, 3)), f)
read_dimacs(f)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 1 2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] -1  3
#> 
sat_solve(read_dimacs(f))
#> <zusat_solution> sat  (3 variables, 2 active clauses, 0.000s)
#>  variable value
#>         1  TRUE
#>         2  TRUE
#>         3  TRUE
